title: Raw approve() call in ClaimArbitrage permanently blocks execution for USDT-like reward tokens
description: ClaimArbitrage uses IERC20(rewardToken_).approve(address(sya), p.rewardTokenNeeded) at line 184 (raw approve instead of forceApprove). USDT requires allowance to be 0 before setting a new non-zero value. After first execution, residual allowance persists, causing subsequent approve() calls to revert permanently. Same issue in SYA's approvePhlimbo() at line 482. The contract imports SafeERC20 but uses raw approve() for these calls.
impact: If USDT is set as reward token, ClaimArbitrage permanently broken after first execution. Yield distribution through ClaimArbitrage is permanently blocked. USDT is explicitly in-scope per C4 rules.
attack_path: USDT is configured as the reward token
First execution of ClaimArbitrage succeeds, leaves residual allowance > 0
Second execution calls approve() with new non-zero value
USDT reverts because existing allowance is not zero
ClaimArbitrage permanently bricked for USDT reward token
recommendation: Replace with SafeERC20.forceApprove(): `IERC20(rewardToken_).forceApprove(address(sya), p.rewardTokenNeeded)`. Same fix for SYA line 482.
